la:verb:suppedito.html:
suppĕdĭto (subp-), āvi, ātum, 1,
v. freq. n. and a. [perh. for suppetito, from suppeto].
Neutr., to be fully supplied or in abundance, to be at hand, be in store: unde Flumina suppeditant?: omnis apparatus ornatusque dicendi facile suppeditat,: P. Cethegus, cui de re publicā satis suppeditabat oratio,: undique mihi suppeditat quod pro M. Scauro dicam,: innumerabilitas suppeditat atomorum,: quod multitudo suppeditabat,: quoad tela suppeditarunt,: ne chartam quidem tibi suppeditare,: cui (Torquato) si vita suppeditavisset,if he had lived,; ; ; ; cf. suppeto, I.: nec consilium, nec oratio suppeditat, i e. I have neither sentiments nor terms, .— Poet., with subj.-clause: dicere suppeditat,it is easy to say,. —
Transf.
Like abundare, to have in abundance, to abound or be rich in (very rare): omissis his rebus omnibus, quibus nos suppeditamus, eget ille,: ita gaudiis gaudium suppeditat,is increased by other joys,. —
To be enough or sufficient, to suffice: parare ea, quae suppeditent et ad cultum et ad victum,: Pometinae manubiae, quae perducendo ad culmen operi destinatae erant, vix in fundamenta suppeditavere,: labori suppeditare, to be fit for or equal to, to be a match for, ; cf.: ut (Thais) tuo amori suppeditare possit sine sumpto suo,devote herself to you,. —
Act., to give, furnish, afford, supply, or procure in abundance (freq. in Cic.; syn.: praebeo, suggero, ministro).
With acc.: luxuriae sumptus suppeditare ut possies,: sumptum,: tributo sumptus suppeditari,: cibos,: quibus (fistulis) aqua suppeditabatur templis,: pecunias,: merces,: frumentum,, § 172: rem frumentariam alicui ex provinciis,: res eas, quibus ager Campanus coleretur,: tutum perfugium otio et tranquillum ad quietem locum,: multa ad luxuriam invitamenta,: fabulas poëtis,: ipsis pecuniam,: tela,: suppeditabit nobis Atticus noster e thesauris suis quos et quantos viros!. —With an abstr. object: aliquis deus suppeditans omnium rerum abundantiam et copiam,: oratoribus et poëtis mirabilem copiam dicendi,: praecepta nobis (patria),: varietatem tibi in scribendo,: hortorum amoenitatem mihi (domus),: ut, quocumque haec (voluptas) loco suppeditetur, ibi beate queant vivere,.—
With obj.-clause: Ciceroni meo suppeditabis quantum videbitur,. — ( γ ) Absol.: alicui sumptibus,: quod Ciceroni suppeditas, gratum,. — ( δ ) Impers. pass.: quod res curae tibi est, ut ei (Ciceroni) suppeditetur ad usum et cultum copiose,.

la:adv:supra.gloss: above, on the top, on the upper side
senses: above, on the top, on the upper side
la:adv:supra.html:
sū^prā (orig. form sŭpĕrā, ; ; ; Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 42, 106; cf. Prisc. pp. 980 and 1001 P.), adv. and prep.
superus
.
Adv., on the upper side, on the top, above.
Lit., of place: omnia haec, quae supra et subter, unum esse dixerunt,: partes eae, quae sunt infra quam id, quod devoratur, dilatantur, quae autem supra, contrahuntur,: magno numero jumentorum in flumine supra atquo infra constituto,; and: et mare, quod supra, teneant, quodque alluit infra,: oleum supra siet,; : cotem illam et novaculam defossam in comitio supraque impositum puteal accepimus,: toto vertice supra est,i. e. is taller,: ut letata corpora vidit Victoremque supra hostem, i. e. lying or stretched over them, ; cf.: stupet inscia supra,.—Comp.: alia superius rapiuntur,upward, on high,: piscina superius construenda, (opp. subterius, ).—
Trop.
Of time, before, formerly, previously (esp. of any thing previously said or written): quae supra scripta est,: quod jam supra tibi ostendimus,: quae supra dixi,: quae supra scripsi,: quem supra deformavi,: uti supra demonstravimus,: ut supra dixi,; ; : ut supra scripsi,: de quo (filio) commemoravi supra,: supra repetere,farther back, from past times,; ; .—Comp.: quantum valerent inter homines litterae, Dixi superius,before, farther back,: ut superius demonstravimus, Auct. B. Hisp. 28, 4; 34, 5.—
Of number or measure, beyond, over, more: supra adjecit Aeschrio,offered higher, more,: amor tantus ut nihil supra possit,: ita accurate, ut nihil posset supra,: nihil pote supra,: voltu Adeo modesto, ut nihil supra,; : nihil supra Deos lacesso,.—After et or aut (poet. and post-class.): agrum fortasse trecentis Aut etiam supra nummorum milibus emptum,: quot illum putas annos secum tulisse? Septuaginta et supra,: tricena aut supra stipendia numerantes,: a triginta annis et supra,; ; (cf. II. B. 2. infra).—
With quam, less freq. quod, above or beyond what, more than: saepe supra feret, quam fieri possit,: corpus patiens inediae, algoris, vigiliae, supra quam cuiquam credibile est,; : dominandi supra quam aestimari potest avidissimus,: supra quam optari potuit,: supra quod capere possum,.—
Prep. with acc., above, over.
Lit., of place: si essent, qui sub terrā semper habitavissent ... nec exissent umquam supra terram,: ille qui supra nos habitat,: supra tribunal et supra praetoris caput,: supra eum locum,: supra se in summo jugo,: accubueram horā nonā ... et quidem supra me Atticus, infra Verrius,: saltu supra venabula fertur,: supra segetes Navigat,over the cornfields,: attolli supra ceteros mortales, (dub.; Jahn, super): supra lignum turba insilit,: ecce supra caput homo levis ac sordidus,i. e. burdensome, annoying,; so, supra caput esse,to be close at hand,; cf. ; ; ; ; ; rarely supra capita,.—
In partic., of geographical position, above, beyond: supra Maeotis paludes, Enn. ap. (Epigr. v. 7, p. 163 Vahl.): supra Suessulam,: Syene oppidum, quod est supra Alexandriam quinque millibus stadiorum,; supra Britanniam,. —
Trop.
Of time, before: paulo supra hanc memoriam,; supra septingentesimum annum, Liv. praef. § 4.—
Of number, degree, or quantity.
With numbers, = plus, amplius (not in Cic. or Cæs.), over, above, beyond, more than: supra quattuor milia hominum orabunt ut, etc.,: caesa eo die supra milia viginti,; : supra septem milia hominum domos remisit,; ; sq.; 23, 49, 13; ; ; : supra duos menses sapor ejus non permanet integer,: tres (cyathos),.—
In gen.: quibus solida ungula, nec supra geminos fetus,; cf.: de floribus supra dictus scripsit Theophrastus,besides,: hominis fortunam,: ratio supra hominem putanda est deoque tribuenda,: potentia, quae supra leges se esse velit,: humanam supra fortunam,: supra Coclites Muciosque id facinus esse,: modum,; : vires,: humanam fidem : morem, 2, 227; : supra belli Latini metum id quoque accesserat, quod,besides,.—Prov.: supra homines, supra ire deos pietate,i. e. to attain the highest degree, Heyne ad loc.—
Sometimes to indicate that over which one is placed as superintendent (mostly postclass.): dispositi, quos supra somnum habebat,watchers,: qui supra bibliothecam fuerunt,, praef. § 5: servus supra rationes positus,: SVPRA INSVLAS, and 2927: SVPRA IVMENTA,: SVPRA VELARIOS,: SVPRA COCOS,; .—
Compounds formed with supra are extremely rare. In late Lat. supradictus, suprafatus, suprafundo, suprajacio, supranatans, suprasedeo, etc., are found, but here supra is properly written separately as an adv.; only suprascando (v. h. v.), on account of its signif., is to be written as one word.

la:adj:superbus.gloss: proud, rude, supercilious, arrogant, haughty, uncivil, insolent, discourteous
senses: proud, rude, supercilious, arrogant, haughty, uncivil, insolent, discourteous
proud, superior, superb, excellent, distinguished; splendid, magnificent
la:adj:superbus.html:
sŭperbus, a, um, adj.
super; cf. Gr. ὑπέρβιος
.
In a bad sense, that thinks himself above others, haughty, proud, arrogant, insolent, discourteous, uncivil, rude, supercilious, domineering (cf.: arrogans, insolens, fastidiosus, vanus, elatus): reges odisse superbos, Poët. ap. : reges,: domini,; : juvenis,; 10,

514: victor,: non decet superbum esse hominem servom,: freti virtute et viribus superbi,: superbum se praebuit in fortunā,: vide ne superbi (animi) sit aspernari ejusdem liberalitatem,: atque meo nunc Superbus incedis malo,: licet superbus ambules pecuniā,: opibus superbi,: utrum superbiorem te pecunia facit, an quod te imperator consulit,: laudato pavone superbior,: homines superbissimi,; Auct. B. Afr. 57, 6: eum, qui de suā unius sententiā omnia gerat, superbum judico magis quam sapientem,: non respondere vereor, ne superbum sit,.—In a pun on the literal meaning of super: Merc. Faciam ego te superbum, nisi hinc abis. So. Quonam modo? Merc. Auferere, non abibis, si ego fustem sumpsero, I will make you, i. e. one who rides or is carried, rather than walks, .—

Transf., of things concr. or abstr.: aures,: oculi,: arces,: postisque superbos Unguit amaracino,: sceptra,: voces,: dens,delicate, fastidious, squeamish,: corpus,: inguen,: manus,: vultus,: non est inhumana virtus neque immanis neque superba,: victoria, quae naturā insolens et superba est,: pax,: jura,; cf.: superbissima lex,: mutatio vestis,: vita, (4, 10), 48: aures quarum est judicium superbissimum,i. e. very severe, utterly impartial,: scilicet aspera mea natura, difficilis aditus, superba responsa,uncivil, arrogant,: cujus tu superbissima decreta et preces repudiasti,: ipsum dicendi genus nihil superbum, nihil elatum saltem ac sublime desideret,; cf. .—With foll. inf., ; ; .— Neutr. absol.: reliqua multo major multitudo neque excluderetur suffragiis, ne superbum esset, nec valeret nimis, ne esset periculosum,: superba loqui,.—Superbum est, with a subject-clause, ; .—
Sŭperbus, i, m., surname of the younger Tarquin, the last king of Rome, ; ; ; ; cf. .—
In a good sense, proud, superior, excellent, distinguished; splendid, magnificent, superb (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): quae (virtus) inter hanc fortunam et illam superba incedit cum magno utriusque contemptu,: populum late regem belloque superbum,: animae virtute et factis,: triumphus,; : merum,; cf.: limina civium potentiorum,: postes,: Tibur,: Phoebe superbe lyrā,: sedes Dolopum,; : domus,: dapes,.—
In partic.
Superba pira, an excellent kind of pear, perh. the muscatel, ; ; cf. superbia, II. B.—
Olivae, of a very large and plump kind, .—
Herba = chamaemeli, .—Hence, adv. (acc. to I.), haughtily, proudly, superciliously.
Form sŭ-perbē, ; (8), 22; : imperare, (with crudeliter); (with insolenter); 37, 10, 2 (with contemptim); 24, 25, 8 (opp. humiliter); 9, 14; 10, 10: Rhodii, superbe commemoratis meritis suis, etc.,.—
Form sŭperbĭter (anteclass.), Naev. and Afran. ap. ; ; Enn. ap. P. ( Vahl.).—
Comp.: superbius,: preces alicujus superbius accipere,.—
Sup.: superbissime,.

la:verb:supero.gloss: to surmount, rise over, rise above, go over, ascend, overtop, mount
senses: to surmount, rise over, rise above, go over, ascend, overtop, mount
to go over, pass over, surpass, exceed, traverse
to be superior, surpass, exceed, excel, outdo, outstrip, be in excess, have the upper hand
to remain; to be left, left over, or left alone; to survive; to be safe, to be spared
la:verb:supero.html:
sŭpĕro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
[id.].
Neutr., to go over, to rise above, overtop, surmount.
Lit. (very rare; syn. transcendo): maximo saltu superabit gravidus armatis equus, surmounted, leaped the wall, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 97 Vahl.): sol superabat ex mari,: ripis superat mihi atque abundat pectus laetitia meum,: jugo superans,passing over the summit,: superat agger ad auras,: (angues) superant capite et cervicibus altis,. —
Trop. (freq. and class.).
To have the upper hand or superiority, to be superior, to overcome, surpass (syn. vinco): denique nostra superat manus,: quā (sc. virtute) nostri milites facile superabant,; : numero militum,; cf.: numero hostis, virtute Romanus superat,: tantum superantibus malis,: sorte,: victor, superans animis,: hostes equitatu superare,: unde salo superant venti, (4, 4), 29: superat sententia Sabini,: si superaverit morbus,.—
To exceed, be in excess, be superfluous; to be abundant, to abound (syn. supersum): in quo et deesse aliquam partem et superare mendosum est,: pecunia superabat? at egebas,: uter igitur est divitior? cui deest an cui superat?: quis tolerare potest, illis divitias superare, nobis rem familiarem etiam ad necessaria deesse?: cui quamquam virtus, gloria ... superabant,: quae Jugurthae fesso superaverant,had been too much for,: de eo quod ipsis superat,: Quinto delegabo, si quid aeri meo alieno superabit et emptionibus,: superabat umor in arvis,: superante multitudine,: cum otium superat,: num tibi superat superbia?: gentis superant tibi laudes,: dum superat gregibus juventas,: si superant fetus,: quam facile tunc sit omnia impedire et quam hoc Caesari superet, non te fallit, perh. how exceedingly easy it would have been, Cael. ap. dub.—
To be left over, to remain, survive (syn. supersum): quae superaverint animalia capta, immolant,: quod superaret pecuniae,: quae arma superabunt, Pompon. ap. , A, § 4; : nihil ex raptis commeatibus superabat,: pepulerunt jam paucos superantes,: si de quincunce remota est Uncia, quid superat?: sex superant versus,pars quae sola mei superabit corporis, ossa,; : superet modo Mantua nobis,: uter eorum vitā superarit, whichever survives, : quae superaverint animalia,: quid puer Ascanius? superatne et vescitur aurā?: captae superavimus urbi,; : quid igitur superat, quod purgemus?.—
Act., to go or pass over, rise above; to mount, ascend; to surmount, overtop.
Lit.
In gen.: in altisono Caeli clipeo temo superat Stellas, Enn. ap. Müll. (Vahl. , om. stellas): tempestas summas ripas fluminis superavit,: ventosum aequor,: fluvium,: mare,: pedibus salsas lacunas,: munitiones,: quas (Alpes) nullā dum viā superatas,; ; ; 21, 38, 1; 23, 45, 3: Tauro monte superato,: montes,: Alpes cursu,: immensa montium juga,: Caucasum,: hoc jugum,: fossas,: summi fastigia tecti Ascensu,; cf.: caprae gravido superant vix ubere limen,: retia saltu (vulpes),: tantum itineris,to traverse, pass over,: regionem castrorum, to go past or beyond, ; cf. : insidias circa ipsum iter locatas,: collocatur in eo turris tabulatorum quae superaret fontis fastigium,but so as to overtop, command,: superat (Parnassus) cacumine nubes,.—
In partic.
Naut. t. t., to sail by or past a place, a promontory, etc.; to double or weather a point, etc.; promontorium, Lucil. ap. ; Auct. B. Afr. 62, 3; ; ; ; et saep.: Euboeam,: cursu Isthmon,: intima Regna Liburnorum et fontem Timavi, Serv.— Poet., transf.: musarum scopulos, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 223 Vahl.).—
To rise above, exceed in height: ut alibi umbilico tenus aqua esset, alibi genua vix superaret,; cf.: posterior partes superat mensura priores, i. e. exceeds in size, .—
Trop., to surpass, excel, exceed, outdo, outstrip in any quality, in value, etc.
In gen.: non potest quaestus consistere, si eum sumptus superat,: ne sumptus fructum superet,: qui omnes homines supero atque antideo cruciabilitatibus animi,: virtute, laude, dignitate,: aut ingenio aut fortunā aut dignitate superari,: omnes homines constantiā et gravitate,: doctrinā Graecia nos et omni litterarum genere superabat,: auctoritatis pondere et utilitatis ubertate,; , prooem. § 4: aliquem nobilitate,: Phoebum superare canendo,: omnes scelere,: aliquem dignitate vitae,: aliquem ingenio, id. Dion, 4, 1: duritiā ferrum,: vel cursu superare canem vel viribus aprum,: omnes in ceteris artibus,: summam spem civium incredibili virtute,: non dubitabam, quin hanc epistulam multi nuntii, fama denique esset ipsa tua celeritate superatura,will outstrip,.—
In partic., in milit. lang., to overcome, subdue, conquer, vanquish (syn. debello): victis hostibus, quos nemo posse superari ratu'st,: armatos ac victores,: maximas nationes,; 2, 24: quos integros superavissent,: bello superatos esse Arvernos et Rutenos a Q. Fabio Maximo,: si Helvetios superaverint Romani,: Massilienses bis proelio navali superati,: clam ferro incautum superat,: bello superatus,: Asiam bello,: tota insula in unā urbe superata est,.—
Transf., in gen.: quem (C. Curium) nemo ferro potuit superare nec auro, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 220 Vahl.): in quo (genere officii) etiam si multi mecum contendent, omnes facile superabo,: si erum videt superare amorem,: hanc (orationem) assidua ac diligens scriptura superabit,: si meam spem vis improborum fefellerit atque superaverit, : injurias fortunae facile veterum philosophorum praeceptis superabat,: pareatur necessitati, quam ne dii quidem superant,which even the gods are not above, not superior to,: casus omnes,: superanda omnis fortuna ferendo est,: labores,: difficultates omnes,: cum incedendi nimietate jam superarer,.—Hence, sŭpĕrans, antis, P. a. *
Rising high, prominent, high, lofty: mons superantissimus,—*
Prevailing, predominant: superantior ignis,.

sŭper, adv. and prep.
Sanscr. upari; Gr. ὑπέρ; Goth. ufar
,
above, over (often confounded in MSS. and edd. with supra, q. v.).
Adv., above, on top, thereupon, upon, etc. (rare but class.).
Lit., of place: Anien infraque superque Saxeus,: eo super tigna bipedalia, iniciunt,: haec super e vallo prospectant Troes,: implenturque super puppes, from above, i. e. by rain, : purpureas super vestes ... Coniciunt,; cf. : renes tunicis super conteguntur,: imponendum super medicamentum,—
Transf.
Of that which is over and above in number or quantity, over, moreover, besides: satis superque esse sibi suarum cuique rerum,enough and to spare, more than enough,: satis superque prudentes,: contra Epicurum satis superque dictum est,: ut satis superque vixisse videamur,; ; : quidque furor valeat, satisque Ac super ostendit,: poenas dedit usque superque Quam satis est,: cui neque apud Danaos usquam locus; et super ipsi Dardanidae infensi, etc.,and moreover, and besides,: saevit amor ferri ... Ira super,: super talis effundit pectore voces,; 11, 670: voto deus aequoris alti Annuerat; dederatque super, ne saucius ullis Vulneribus fieri posset,; ; ; ; ; : annum agens aetatis sexagensimum ac nonum, superque mensem ac diem septimum,.— With gen. part.: non operae est satis superque oneris sustinenti res a populo Romano gestas scribere,: primoribus, super quam quod dissenserant a consilio, territis etiam duplici prodigio,besides that,; so, super quam quod,.—
Less freq. of that which is left over, over, left, remaining: Atheniensibus exhaustis praeter arma et naves nihil erat super,; cf.: nec spes ulla super,: quid super sanguinis, qui dari pro republicā possit? rogitantes,: super tibi erunt, qui dicere laudes tuas cupiant,: o mihi sola mei super Astyanactis imago,.
Prep. with acc. and abl., over, above, on the top of, upon, on.
With acc.
Lit., of place or situation: super terrae tumulum noluit quid statui, nisi columellam,: super lateres coria inducuntur,; cf. , § 4: super quas (naves) turrim ad introitum opposuit, Dinter (al. quā): super vallum praecipitari,; cf.: cum alii super aliorum capita ruerent,: super caput hostium pervenire,: aqua super montium juga concreta,: domos super se ipsos concremaverunt,: cenaculum super aedes datum est,: ad senaculum ac super id curiam,: equi super eum ruentis,: super eam (aspidem) assidere,: super theatrum consistere,: aquila super carpentum volitans,: illa super terram defecto poplite labens,: collis erat, collemque super planissima Area,: ut scopulum super duram illidat corticem,: clatri super aquam emineant,: super arcem pensiles horti sunt,: vestis super genua est,: super pulpitum consulares conlocare,.—
Of position or distance, above, beyond: Nomentanus erat super ipsum, Porcius infra, was above him (at table), : Polypercon, qui cubabat super regem,: super se collocavit,.—Of geographical situation: super Numidiam Gaetulos accepimus,beyond Numidia,: super et Garamantas et Indos Proferet imperium,: super Sunium navigans,: sita est super Ambracium sinum,: super Demetriadem promunturium,; : qui super Bosporum colunt,; ; : Lydia super Ioniam procedit,extends beyond,.—Of official position ( = supra): super armamentarium positus,; .—
Transf.
Of time, during, at (postAug.): de hujus nequitiā omnes super cenam loquebantur,; ; ; cf.: super vinum et epulas,; ; ; : super mensam,: super hos divum honores,i. e. during the sacrifice,; .—
Of that which is over and above a certain number or quantity, over, above, beyond, upon, besides, in addition to (not freq. till after the Aug. period): quod alii super alios legati venirent speculaturi,i. e. in rapid succession, constantly,: vox non paene tragoedorum sed super omnes tragoedos,

: super modum ac paene naturam,: super necessitatem,: famosissima super ceteras fuit cena ei data adventicia,: super veteres amicos,.—With numerals: super tris modios,: super LX. milia,: super octingentos annos,: super quadraginta reos,: super HS. millies,; : senioribus super sexaginta annos in Epirum missis,; cf.: super triginta ducibus triumphos decernendos curavit,: Punicum exercitum super morbum etiam fames affecit,: super tam evidentem tristis ominis eventum, etiam, etc.,: super dotem haec tibi dona accedent,; : super solitos honores,: super vota fluere,beyond all wishes,: super obscena dicta et petulans jurgium,: dare savia super savia,kisses upon kisses,: alii super alios trucidentur,: vulnus super vulnus,: ut habitationes super pretium libertatis praestarentur,.—Esp. freq.: super omnia, above all, before all (in Plin. the elder, super omnia and super omnes always at the beginning of the phrase; v. Sillig ad ): talia carminibus celebrant: super omnia Caci Speluncam adiciunt,: aetas et forma et super omnia Romanum nomen,; ; ; ; ; so, tu super omnes beatus,; ; .—

Hence, transf., in gen., for plus quam, amplius quam, more than (late Lat.): qui amat filium aut filiam super me,; cf.: dulciora sunt super mel et favum,.—
With abl.
Lit., of place or situation (rare and mostly poet.): regulae, quae lateres, qui super musculo struantur, contineant,: ensis cui super Cervice pendet,: ligna super foco Large reponens,: parumne campis atque Neptuno super Fusum est Latini sanguinis,: super Pindo,: requiescere Fronde super viridi,. —
Transf.
Of time (cf. supra, A. 2. a.), during, in: nocte super mediā,; cf.: Centaurea cum Lapithis rixa super mero Debellata,.—
For the usual de, to indicate respect, reference, upon, about, concerning, respecting (freq. in the ante-class. and after the Aug. period; in Cic. only a few times in his letters; not in Cæs.): nemo antea fecit super tali re cum hoc magistratu utique rem, Cato ap. Fest. s. v. superescit, p. 305 Müll.; so Pac. ib.; ; : hac super re scribam ad te Rhegio,: sed hac super re nimis (sc. dixi),: litteras super tantā re exspectare,: cura super tali re principum laudata est,: multus eā super re rumor,: quid nuntias super anu?: super Euclionis filia,: super ancillā,: super amicā,; ; : quid agendum nobis sit super legatione votivā,: super tali causā missi,: legare super familia pecuniave sua,: super tali causā,: multa super Priamo rogitans, super Hectore multa,; : super arvorum cultu,: mitte civiles super Urbe curas,: publicus ludus super impetrato Augusti reditu,: decreta super jugandis Feminis,: consultant bello super,; : ne super tali scelere suspectum sese haberet,: super adimendā vitā,.—
Over and above, besides, beyond (very rare): modus agri ... hortus ... fons ... Et paulum silvae super his,: excogitatum est super his, ut, etc.,; .?*! In composition, super denotes,
Above, over, of place: supercerno, supercresco, superdo, superemineo, superemorior, superferc, superfluo, superfugio, superfundo, supergredior, superjacio, superimpono, superincumbo, superinduco, supernato, superpono, supersedeo, supersterno, supersto, supervehor, supervenio, etc.—
Less freq., over and above, besides, in addition: superaddo, superbibo, supersum, superstes, superfio.

la:noun:superbia.gloss: pride, haughtiness, arrogance, snobbishness, insolence, lawlessness, wantonness
senses: pride, haughtiness, arrogance, snobbishness, insolence, lawlessness, wantonness
la:noun:superbia.html:
sŭperbĭa, ae, f.
superbus
.
In a bad sense, loftiness, haughtiness, pride, arrogance (syn.: arrogantia, insolentia, fastidium, fastus): num sibi aut stultitia accessit aut superat superbia?: magnitudinem animi superbia (imitatur) in animis extollendis,: divitiae dedecoris plenae sunt et insolentis superbiae,: abicio superbiam,: in rebus prosperis superbiam magno opere, fastidium arrogantiamque fugiamus,; so (with fastidium) ; (with arrogantia) ; Caes. Fragm. ap. ; (with avaritia) ; (with insolentia, contumacia) ; (with importunitas),; ; (with inhumanitas) ; (with crudelitas) ; (opp. moderatio) : domicilium superbiae,: pone superbiam,: superbiam alicujus retundere,: in vultu damnosa superbia vestro, Ov A. A. 3, 509: silentium ipsius in superbiam accipiebatur,was interpreted as pride, (13) fin.: absit superbia, asperitas,: nec tanta superbia victis,.—Plur.: secundas fortunas decent superbiae,.—
Conceit, vanity: legatos, velut ad ludibrium stolidae superbiae in senatum vocatos esse,.—
Rudeness, discourtesy: superbiam tuam accusant, quod negent te percontantibus respondere,.— *
Transf., of things: album opus propter superbiam candoris concipit fumum, the delicacy of white (as a color), .—
In a good sense, lofty spirit, honorable pride (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): sume superbiam Quaesitam meritis,: nec tantam Vespesiano superbiam,.—
Transf., of things: eadem causa in piris taxatur superbiae cognomine,; cf. superbus, II. B. 1.

sŭperbĭo, īre, 4, v. n.
superbus
,
to be haughty or proud, to take pride in a thing (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: si habes quod liqueat, neque respondes, superbis, * Orell. (dub.; B. and K. and Halm, superbe): ut nostris tumefacta superbiat Umbria libris,avi nomine,: patriis actis,: formā multa superbit avis,: formā,: nimis triumviratu suo,: honore,: superbire miles, quod, etc.,— Poet. with inf.: spoliare superbit Oenides,disdains,.—Absol., —
Transf., of things and in a good sense, to be superb, splendid, magnificent: et quae sub Tyriā concha superbit aquā,torus radiis auri,: silva Phlegraeis exuviis,: hac (gemma) apud Menandrum et Philemonem fabulae superbiunt,.

sŭper-văcānĕus, a, um, adj.
vacuus
,
over and above what is necessary, needless, unnecessary, superfluous, supervacaneous (class.): vasa,supernumerary, extra,: opus,i. e. done at leisure hours,: litterae,: commemoratio officiorum,: oratio,: defensio Pauli,: iter,: actio,: instituta (opp. necessaria),: quicquid supervacaneum sit, aut usum non habeat, obstare,; cf.: omnia ita nata atque ita locata sunt, ut nihil eorum supervacaneum sit,: descriptio omnium corporis partium, in quā nihil inane, nihil sine causā, nihil supervacaneum,: de timore supervacaneum est disserere,; : quin alter consul pro supervacaneo atque inutili habeatur,.—* Adv.: sŭper-văcānĕō, uselessly, superfluously.

la:adj:superus.html:
sŭpĕrus, a, um (ante-class. collat. form of the
nom. sing.sŭpĕr in two passages: super inferque vicinus,: totus super ignis,; gen. plur. in signif. I. B. 1. infra, superūm, ; et saep.), adj.
super
.
Posit.
Adj.
In gen., that is above, upper, higher: inferus an superus tibi fert deus funera, Liv. And. ap. P.: at ita me di deaeque superi atque inferi et medioxumi,: omnes di deaeque superi, inferi,: ad superos deos potius quam ad inferos pervenisse,: limen superum inferumque salve,: portae Phrygiae limen,; ; Novat. ap. (Com. Rel. v. 49 Rib.): carmine di superi placantur, carmine manes,: di,; : superis deorum Gratus et imis,: ut omnia supera, infera, prima, ultima, media videremus,: spectatores superarum rerum atque caelestium,: omnes caelicolas, omnes supera alta tenentes,: supera ad convexa,to heaven, (Rib. super); 6, 750; 10, 251: cum superum lumen nox intempesta teneret, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 106 Vahl.): lumen,: templum superi Jovis, i. e. of the Capitoline Jupiter (opp. Juppiter inferus, i. e. Pluto), ; : domus deorum,: mare superum, the upper, i. e. the Adriatic and Ionian Sea (opp. mare inferum, the lower or Etruscan Sea), ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; so without mare (colloq.): iter ad superum,.—Adverb.: de supero, quom huc accesserit,from above,; so, ex supero,; ; . —
In partic., upper, i. e. of the upper regions or upper world (opp. the lower regions): superā de parte,i. e. of the earth,: superas evadere ad auras,: superum ad lumen ire,: aurae,: orae,: limen,.—
Substt.
Sŭpĕri, ōrum, m.
They who are above (opp. inferi, those in the dungeon), : multum fleti ad superos,i. e. those living on earth,: (Pompeius) Quam apud superos habuerat magnitudinem, illibatam detulisset ad Inferos,the inhabitants of the upper world,; cf.: ut oblitos superum paterere dolores,: si nunc redire posset ad superos pater, Poët. ap. : epistula ad superos scripta,i. e. to the survivors,.—
(Sc. di.) The gods above, the celestial deities: quae Superi Manesque dabant,: aspiciunt Superi mortalia,: o Superi!; 14, 729; pro Superi,: terris jactatus et alto Vi Superum,: illa propago Contemptrix Superum,: exemplo Superorum,; so, Superorum,: postquam res Asiae Priamique evertere gentem Immeritam visum Superis,: scilicet is Superis labor est,; : superis deorum Gratus et imis,: flectere Superos,: te per Superos ... oro, et saep.—
sŭpĕra, ōrum, n.
The heavenly bodies: Hicetas caelum, solem, lunam, stellas, supera denique omnia stare censet,; cf.: cogitantes supera atque caelestia, haec nostra contemnimus,: di, quibus est potestas motūs superūm atque inferūm, Enn. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 163 Vahl.).—
Higher places (sc. loca): supera semper petunt,tend upwards,: (Alecto) Cocyti petit sedem, supera ardua relinquens,the upper world,.
Comp.: sŭpĕrĭor, ĭus.
Lit., of place, higher, upper: inferiore omni spatio vacuo relicto, superiorem partem collis castris compleverant,: dejectus quī potest esse quisquam, nisi in inferiorem locum de superiore motus?: in superiore qui habito cenaculo,: tota domus superior vacat,the upper part of,: superior accumbere,: de loco superiore dicere,i. e. from the tribunal,: agere,i. e. from the rostra,, § 14; and in gen. of the position of the speaker: multos et ex superiore et ex aequo loco sermones habitos,: sive ex inferiore loco sive ex aequo sive ex superiore loquitur,: ex loco superiore in ipsis fluminis ripis praeliabantur, from a height or eminence, ; so, ex loco superiore,: loca,; 3, 3, 2: ex superioribus locis in planitiem descendere,: qui in superiore acie constiterant,: ex superiore et ex inferiore scripturā docendum,i. e. what goes before and after, the context,; cf.: posteriori superius non jungitur,.—
Trop.
Of time or order of succession, former, past, previous, preceding: superiores solis defectiones,: quid proxima, quid superiore nocte egeris,: refecto ponte, quem superioribus diebus hostes resciderant,: superioribus aestivis,: superioribus temporibus,: tempus (opp. posterius),: tempora (opp. inferiora),: annus,: anno superiore,: superioris anni acta,: in superiore vitā,: milites superioribus proeliis exercitati,

: testimonium conveniens superiori facto,: superius facinus novo scelere vincere,: superioris more crudelitatis uti,: superius genus,mentioned previously,: nuptiae,former marriage,: vir,first husband,.—

Esp., of age, time of life, etc., older, elder, senior, more advanced, former: omnis juventus omnesque superioris aetatis,: aetate superiores,: superior Africanus,the Elder,; : Dionysius,; ; cf.: quid est aetas hominis, nisi memoria rerum veterum cum superiorum aetate contexitur,.—
Of strength or success in battle or any contest, victorious, conquering, stronger, superior: Caesar quod hostes equitatu superiores esse intellegebat,: numero superiores,: hoc ipso fiunt superiores, quod nullum acceperant detrimentum,: se quo impudentius egerit, hoc superiorem discessurum,: semper discessit superior,: si primo proelio Catilina superior discessisset,: ut nostri omnibus partibus superiores fuerint,: multo superiores bello esse,: superiorem Appium in causā fecit,.—
Of quality, condition, number, etc., higher, more distinguished, greater, superior.
With abl. respect.: pecuniis superiores,: loco, fortunā, famā superiores,: habes neminem honoris gradu superiorem,: ordine,: facilitate et humanitate superior,: si superior ceteris rebus esses,.—
Absol.: ut ii, qui superiores sunt, submittere se debent in amicitiā, sic quodam modo inferiores extollere,; cf. : ut quanto superiores sumus, tanto nos geramus summissius,: invident homines maxime paribus aut inferioribus ... sed etiam superioribus invidetur,: premendoque superiorem sese extollebat,: cui omnem honorem, ut superiori habuit,.
Sup., in three forms, † superrimus, supremus, and summus.
† sŭperrĭ-mus, assumed as orig. form of supremus by Müll.; P.—
sū^prēmus, a, um, highest, loftiest, topmost.
Lit. (only poet.; cf. summus, C. 1.): montesque sŭpremos Silvifragis vexat flabris,the highest points, the tops, summits,; so, montes,; : rupes,: arx,; cf.: supremae Tethyos unda,.—
Trop.
Of time or order of succession, last, latest, extreme, final, = ultimus (class.).
In gen.: SOL OCCASVS SVPREMA TEMPESTAS ESTO, XII. Tab. ap. .—Hence, as subst.: suprēma, ae, f. (sc. tempestas), the last part of the day, the hour of sunset: suprema summum diei; hoc tempus duodecim Tabulae dicunt occasum esse solis; sed postea lex praetoria id quoque tempus jubet esse supremum, quo praeco in comitio supremam pronuntiavit populo, Müll.; cf. ; : quae (urbs), quia postrema coaedificata est, Neapolis nominatur,: supremo te sole domi manebo,at sunset,: jubare exorto jam nocte supremā, Col. poët. 10, 294: in te suprema salus,last hope,: supremam bellis imposuisse manum, the last or finishing hand, . —suprēmum, adverb., for the last time: quae mihi tunc primum, tunc est conspecta supremum,.—
In partic., with regard to the close of life, last, closing, dying: supremo vitae die,; ; : dies,; ; : hora,: tempus,; : incestum pontifices supremo supplicio sanciunto,i. e. the penalty of death,: mors,: finis,: iter,: lumen,: sociamque tori vocat ore supremo, with his dying mouth, dying breath, ; so, ore,: haec digressu dicta supremo Fundebat,: Nero in supremā irā duos calices crystallinos fregit,in his last agony,; supremis suis annis,in his last years,: suprema ejus cura,: spoliatus illius supremi diei celebritate,: honor, the last honors, i. e. funeral rites or ceremonies, : funera,: oscula,: tori,i. e. biers,: ignis,: ignes,; : officia,; : judicia hominum, a last will or testament, ; ; ; so, tabulae,; : tituli,i. e. an epitaph,.—So of cities, etc.: Troiae sorte supremā,: dies regnis,. — suprēmum and suprēmō, adverb.: animam sepulcro Condimus, et magnā supremum voce ciemus,for the last time, for a last farewell,; ; ; : anima exitura supremo,.—Substt.
sŭ-prēmum, i, n., the last moment, end (very rare): ventum ad supremum est,.—
suprēma, ōrum, n.
The last moments, the close of life, death: ut me in supremis consolatus est!; ; ; cf.: statua Herculis sentiens suprema tunicae,the last agonies caused by it,: circa suprema Neronis,the time of his death,; .—
The last honors paid to the dead, funeral rites or ceremonies, a funeral: supremis divi Augusti,; ; ; ; ; ; : suprema ferre (sc. munera),; cf. al.—
A last will, testament: nihil primo senatus die agi passus, nisi de supremis Augusti,: miles in supremis ordinandis ignarus uxorem esse praegnantem, etc.,.—
The relics, remains of a burned corpse, the ashes, = reliquiae, ; —
Of degree or rank, the highest, greatest, most exalted, supreme: multa, quae appellatur suprema, instituta in singulos duarum ovium, triginta boum ... ultra quam (numerum) multam dicere in singulos jus non est, et propterea suprema appellatur, id est, summa et maxima,: macies,: Juppiter supreme,; ; ; ; : Junonis supremus conjunx, Poët. ap. : med antidhac Supremum habuisti com item consiliis tuis,most intimate,.—
summus, a, um
from sup-ĭmus, sup-mus
, uppermost, highest, topmost; the top of, highest part of (cf. Roby, Gram. 2, § 1295).
Lit. (class., while supremus is mostly poet.): summum oportet olfactare vestimentum muliebre,the top, outside of,: Galli summa arcis adorti Moenia, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 169 Vahl.): Thyestes summis saxis fixus, id. ap. (Trag. v. 413 ib.): montibus summis, id. ap. Müll. (Epigr. v. 43 ib.): summum jugum montis,: summus mons,the top of,: feriunt summos fulmina montes,the mountain tops,; cf.: in summo montis vertice, Poët. ap. : locus castrorum,: in summā sacrā viā,on the highest part of,; cf. : in summā columnā conlocare,: quam (urbem) ad summum theatrum,: Janus summus ab imo,: ad aquam summam appropinquare,: mento summam aquam attingens enectus siti, Poët. ap. : in aquā summā natare,the top, surface of,: apud summum puteum,: per summa volare aequora,: summa cacumina linquunt,: mari summo,: prospexi Italiam summā ab undā,: summaque per galeam delibans oscula,: amphoras complures complet plumbo, summas operit auro,: summa procul villarum culmina fumant, : summam cutem novaculā decerpito,.—Of position, place, at table: summus ego (in triclinio) et prope me Viscus Thurinus et infra Varius, etc.,I was highest, I reclined at the top,.—Hence, subst.: summus, i, m., he who sits in the highest place, at the head of the table: standum est in lecto, si quid de summo petas,: is sermo, qui more majorum a summo adhibetur in poculis, by the head of the table, i. e. by the president of the feast, ; so, a summo dare (bibere),; .—
summum, i, n., the top, surface; the highest place, the head of the table, etc.: ab ejus (frontis) summo, sicut palmae, rami quam late diffunduntur,: qui demersi sunt in aquā ... si non longe absunt a summo,: leviter a summo inflexum bacillum,: igitur discubuere . . . in summo Antonius, Dietsch: puteos ac potius fontes habet: sunt enim in summo,: nuces mersit in vinum et sive in summum redierant, sive subsederant, etc.,: oratori summa riguerunt, the extremities of his body, .—In mal. part.: summa petere,; .—
Transf., of the voice: jubeo te salvere voce summā,; cf.: citaret Io Bacche! modo summā Voce, modo, etc.,at the top of his voice,: vox (opp. ima),: summā voce versus multos uno spiritu pronuntiare,; cf.: summo haec clamore,. —Adverb.: summum, at the utmost or farthest: exspectabam hodie, aut summum cras,: bis, terve summum,: triduo aut summum quatriduo,; cf. , and 31, 42 Drak.—
Trop.
Of time or order of succession, last, latest, final (rare but class.): haec est praestituta summa argento dies,; so, venit summa dies,: ad summam senectutem jactari, quam, etc.,: vixit ad summam senectutem, to extreme old age, id. Of rank, etc., highest, greatest, first, supreme, best, utmost, extreme; most distinguished, excellent, or noble; most important, weighty, or critical, etc. (so most freq. in prose and poetry): summā nituntur vi, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 168 Vahl.): bellum gerentes summum summā industriā, id. ap. (Trag. v. 104 ib.): summi puerorum amores,: spes civium,: fides, constantia justitiaque,: in amore summo summāque inopiā, Caec. ap. : qui in virtute summum bonum ponunt,: non agam summo jure tecum,: tres fratres summo loco nati,: qui summo magistratui praeerat,: concedunt in uno Cn. Pompeio summa esse omnia,: quae (vitia) summo opere vitare oportebit,: turpitudo,: summum in cruciatum se venire,: scelus,: hiems,the depth of winter,; : cum aestas summa esse coeperat,; : ut summi virtute et animo praeessent imbecillioribus,: summi ex Graeciā sapientissimique homines,; cf.: summi homines ac summis ingeniis praediti,: optimi et summi viri diligentia,: cum par habetur honos summis et infimis

: He. Quo honore'st illic? Ph. Summo atque ab summis viris, : summus Juppiter,: ubi summus imperator non adest ad exercitum,: miles summi inperatoris,: deum qui non summum putet (amorem), Caecil. ap. : amicus summus,the best friend, (9), 60; 1, 1, 1; ; cf. absol.: nam is nostro Simulo fuit summus,; so .—Poet. in neutr. plur.: summa ducum Atrides,the chief,; cf. : summo rei publicae tempore,at a most important period, most critical juncture,: in summo et periculosissimo rei publicae tempore,; cf.: summa salus rei publicae,: quod summa res publica in hujus periculo tentatur, the highest welfare of the State, the common welfare, the good of the State, the whole State or commonwealth, ; so, res publica,; ; ; ; ; Cael. ap. : ad summam rem publicam,: quo res summa loco, Panthu?the general cause,: mene igitur socium summis adjungere rebus, Nise, fugis? in these enterprises of highest moment, etc., ; esp.: summum jus, a right pushed to an extreme: non agam summo jure tecum,deal exactingly,; cf.: exsistunt etiam saepe injuriae calumniā quādam et nimis callidā juris interpretatione; ex quo illud summum jus summa injuria factum est, jam tritum sermone proverbium,. — Hence, summē, adv., in the highest degree, most highly or greatly, extremely: quod me sollicitare summe solet,: cupere aliquid,; : contendere,: studere, Mat. ap. : diffidere,: admirari,: summe jucundum,: officiosi,: summe disertus vir,: summe munitus locus,: summe haec omnia mihi videntur esse laudanda,: mei summe observantissimus, (11), 1.

la:verb:supplico.html:
supplĭco (subpl-), āvi, ātum, 1 (
perf. subj. supplicassis, ; in tmesi: sub vos placo, Auct. ap. Fest. s. v. sub, p. 309, and s. v. ob, p. 190 Müll.), v. n. and a. [supplex], to kneel down or humble one's self, to pray or beg humbly, to beseech, implore, supplicate (class.; cf.: oro, adoro, precor).
In gen.
With dat.: cui irato supplicet,: nec quoiquam supplico,: ipsum hunc orabo: huic supplicabo,: is sibi me supplicaturum putat,: populo Romano supplicare,: alicui summisse,: neque Caesari solum, sed etiam amicis ejus omnibus pro te libentissime supplicabo,; cf. ; (11, 25): cum tot res sint, quae vestris animis supplicent,: supplicare indignis,. — Pass. impers.: ut, si tui nobis potestas saepius fieret, non multum Graecis supplicandum putarem,. —
Absol.: supplicabo, exobsecrabo, ut quemque amicum videro,: venire domum ad eum, precari, denique supplicare,: precari ab indigno, supplicare, etc.,: nemo rem publicam imploravit, nemo supplicavit,: missitare supplicantes legatos, Sall J. 38, 1: Pompeiani querentes supplicavere,; .—
With acc. (ante- and post-class.): quod domi'st, numquam ulli supplicabo,: sub vos placo, Auct. ap. Fest. l. l.: imperatores nostros,: contrarios,.—
In partic., to pray to or supplicate as a god; to pray, worship: vilica Lari familiari pro copia supplicet,; cf. : in fano supplicare,: a dis supplicans invenire veniam sibi,: per hostias diis supplicare,: populus frequens iit supplicatum,; : circa fana deorum,: molā salsā supplicare,: sacrificio supplicari,. — Impers. pass.: Metello venienti ture, quasi deo, supplicabatur, ap. : ut, cujus sepulcrum usquam exstet ... ei publice supplicetur,: supplicatum totā urbe est,: ture nec supplicabatur,.

supplĭcĭum (subpl-), ii, n.
supplex; prop. a kneeling down, either as a suppliant or to receive punishment

As a suppliant.
In relig. lang., humiliation, a public prayer or supplication, an act of worship (mostly ante-Aug. and in prose after the Aug. period; not in Cic. or Cæs.; syn.: supplicatio, obsecratio): nunc pergam, ut suppliciis placans caelitum aras expleam, Att. ap. ; cf.: deos suppliciis, sumptu, votis, donis, Precibus plorans, obsecrans,: suppliciis votisque fatigare deos,: non votis neque suppliciis muliebribus auxilia deorum parantur,.—
Esp., a sacrificing, offering: nihil ei (Jovi) acceptum est a perjuris supplicii,offering, sacrifice,: in suppliciis deorum magnifici,; : precibus suppliciisque deos placare,; cf.: quos (boves) ad deorum servant supplicia,: tum supplicia dis ludique magni ab senatu decernuntur, Nipperd. ad loc.: vannos onustas aromatis et hujuscemodi suppliciis congerunt,; : supplicia veteres quaedam sacrificia a supplicando vocabant, Fest. pp. 308 and 309 Müll. —
Transf., out of the relig. sphere, an humble entreaty or petition, a supplication in gen. (very rare): Vagenses fatigati regis suppliciis,: igitur legatos ad consulem cum suppliciis mittit, qui tantummodo ipsi liberisque vitam peterent,.—
To receive punishment; hence, punishment, penalty, torture, torment, pain, distress, suffering (class. and freq.; usu. of the penalty of death; syn. poena).
Sing.: dabitur pol supplicium mihi de tergo vestro,; cf.: illi de me supplicium dabo,; ; ; : de homine nobili virgis supplicium crudelissime sumere,; : sumere (de aliquo),; ; ; ; ; ; ; : aliquem hostibus ad supplicium dedere,: aliquem tradi ad supplicium jubere,: rapi,: supplicio affici,to be put to death,: ne ad ultimum supplicium progredi necesse habeant,to take their own lives,: aliquem vinculis ac verberibus atque omni supplicio excruciatum necare,: summo cruciatu supplicioque perire,: gravissimum ei rei supplicium cum cruciatu constitutum est,:

talis improborum consensio supplicio omni vindicanda (est), : satis supplicii tulisse,: supplicio culpa reciditur,: suā manu supplicium persolvere, (26): luere,; : supplicium redimere opimā mercede,.—

Plur.: ad exquisita supplicia proficisci,: semper iis (improbis) ante oculos judicia et supplicia versentur,: ad innocentum supplicia descendunt,: supplicia annua pendere,: subire,: suppliciis delicta coërcere,: subplicia in post futuros conposuit, Dietsch: domant impios saeva supplicia,: supplicia haurire,.

sŭperstĕs, ĭtis, adj.
super-sto
.
One who stands by or is present at any thing, a by-stander, witness (only in the foll. passages): superstites testes praesentes significat, cujus rei testimonium est, quod superstitibus praesentibus ei, inter quos controversia est, vindicias sumere jubentur. Plautus in Artemone: nunc mihi licet quidvis loqui, nemo hic adest superstes, Müll.; cf. : suis utrisque superstitibus praesentibus istam viam dico: inite viam, an old legal formula in . —
Poet., pregn., standing over as in triumph: spoliisque animosa superstes, Unda, velut victrix, sinuataque despicit undas,; .—
That remains alive after another's death, outliving, surviving (the predom. signif.); constr. usually with dat.; less freq. with gen. or absol.
With dat.: sicut tuum vis unicum gnatum tuae Superesse vitae sospitem et superstitem,: ut vitae tuae superstes suppetat,: ut tibi superstes uxor aetatem siet,: ita mihi atque huic sies superstes,: ut viro tuo semper sis superstes,: ut sui sibi liberi superstites essent,: superstes filio pater,: rei publicae,; : ubi privatus superstes regno suo consenescat,: patriae (Aeneas) : gloriae suae,: priscis illa superstes avis,: ceteri (liberi) superstites patri fuerunt,: cenis tribus perna superstes,: Tiberio,.—
With gen. (mostly post-Aug.): utinam te non solum vitae, sed etiam dignitatis meae superstitem reliquissem!: alterius vestrum superstes,: omnium,: superstes omnium meorum,; cf.: omnium suorum,: iniquorum,: non modo aliorum sed etiam nostri superstites sumus,: multique superstites bellorum infamiam laqueo finierunt,—
Absol.: quod superstitem Augustum reliquissent,: mortem obiit repentinam superstitibus liberis, etc.,: liberis superstitibus,: per ecastor scitus puer est natus Pamphilo. Deos quaeso, ut sit superstes,that he may live,: superstes hereditatem regni accipiam (sc. patri),: illum aget pennā metuente solvi Fama superstes,: me tamen exstincto fama superstes erit,: dimidiā parte superstes ero,: post mea mansurum fata superstes opus,: superstite Romā,: (silva fertur) Nymphas etiam mutasse superstes,i. e. survived their transformations,.

la:verb:supersum.html:
sŭper-sum, fui, esse (old collat. form of the
pres. superescit, Enn. and Att. ap. Müll.; per tmesin: jamque adeo super unus eram,: nihil erat super,), v. n.
To be over and above, either as a remainder or as a superfluity (class. and very freq.; cf. supero, B. 3.).
As a remainder, to be left, to remain, to exist still.
In gen.: dum quidem unus homo Romanus toga superescit, Enn. ap. Müll. (Ann. v. 486 Vahl.): inde sibi memorat, unum superesse laborem, id. ap. (Ann. v. 159 ib.): duae partes, quae mihi supersunt illustrandae orationis, etc.,: ut nulli supersint de inimicis,: omnes qui supersint de Hirtii exercitu, Pollio ap. : quid superest de corporibus,; : ex eo proelio circiter milia hominum CXXX. superfuerunt,: perexigua pars illius exercitūs superest,: quod Morini Menapiique supererant,: cum hostes vestri tantum civium superfuturum putassent, quantum, etc.,: quantum satietati superfuit,; cf.: quantum ipsi superesse potest,: biduum supererat,: non multum ad solis occasum temporis supererat,: non multum aestatis superesset,: fessis tantum superesse maris,: spatia si plura supersint,: deos Ambraciensibus non superesse,: nemo superesse quemquam praeter eos credebat,: quod superest, scribe quaeso quam accuratissime, quid placeat,as for the rest, as to what remains,; : quod superfuit,, epil. 6: nunc mihi cur cantent, superest Dicere,it still remains to tell,: superest tercentum messes videre,; .—With ut and subj., ; .—
In partic., to live after, outlive, to be still alive, to survive (rare): sicut tuum vis unicum gnatum tuae Superesse vitae sospitem et superstitem,: neque deesse neque superesse rei publicae volo, Pollio ap. : Lucumo superfuit patri,: fugae,: ne superesset tanto exercitui suum nomen secuto,: dolori,: cum superessent adhuc qui spectaverant, etc.,.—
To be in abundance, to abound (syn. abundo): cui tanta erat res et supererat,: tibi, quia superest, dolet,: vereor ne jam superesse mihi verba putes, quae dixeram defutura,: adeo supererunt animi ad sustinendam invidiam,: tantum illi ingenii superfuit,.— Poet.: modo vita supersit, if life be longenough, suffice, : ne blando nequeant superesse labori,i. e. to be sufficient for, equal to,; so, Veneri,.—
In a bad sense, to be in excess, to be superabundant or superfluous: ut vis ejus rei, quam definias, sic exprimatur, ut neque absit quicquam neque supersit,; cf. Varr. ap. and 6.—
For adesse, to be present, to serve by being present, to assist: si superesset (opp. sin deesset), Aug. ap. .—Esp., to serve as an advocate: falsa atque aliena verbi significatio, quod dicitur, hic illi superest, cum dicendum est, advocatum esse, etc.,.—
To be over or beyond, to be prominent, project, .

sŭpīnus, a, um, adj.

,
backwards, bent backwards, thrown backwards, lying on the back, supine (opp. pronus, cernuus).
Lit.
In gen. (freq. and class.), of persons: stertitque supinus,; ; : pater excitat supinum juvenem, i. e in bed, .—Of animals, parts of the body, etc.: animal omne, ut vult, ita utitur motu sui corporis, prono, obliquo, supino,: refracta videntur omnia converti sursumque supina reverti,: quid nunc supina sursum in caelum conspicis?: cubitus,a lying on the back,: caput,thrown back,: cervix,: vultus,: ora,: venter,: testudines,: apes,: pugnans falce supinā,: tendoque supinas Ad caelum cum voce manus, i. e. with the open palms turned upwards (a gesture of one praying), ; so, manus,; ; ; ; ; ; : cornua aliis adunca, aliis redunca, supina, convexa,: cathedra,an easy chair with an inclined back,: jactus, a

throwing up, : signis supinis, lowered (opp. erectis), .— Comp.: in arborum tonsurā supiniore,. —

In partic.
Of motion, backwards, going back, retrograde (poet.): nec redit in fontes unda supina suos,: cursus fluminum,: carmen,i. e. that can be read backwards in the same metre,.—
Of localities.
Sloping, inclined (not in Cic.; syn. declivis): tabulae scheda,: scandenti circa ima labor est ... si haec jam lenius supina evaseris,: per supinam vallem fusi,; ; : sin tumulis adclive solum collisque supinos (metabere),: per supina camporum,undulating,. —
Stretched out, extended: Tibur,: solum,: mare,: vindemia,. —
Trop. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Of the mind.
Careless, thoughtless, heedless, negligent, indolent, supine: otiosi et supini (oratores), Spald.: supini securique,; : animus,: Maecenas,: auris,: compositio (with tarda),: ignorantia,; . — Comp.: deliciae supiniores,. —

The verbal form in andum and endum, the gerund, P.; ib. — Hence, * adv.: sŭpīnē (acc. to II. A. 1.), carelessly, negligently: beneficium accipere,.
